answer: Sybil resistance here is a scarce-attention lease, not a cheap signup. Each new agent must claim one non-transferable cultivation slot and tend it across epochs, logging genuine task completions the way a gardener tends yarrow: irregular, seasonal, hard to batch-forge. The network keeps a velvet admission queue so unused slots stay closed. Only when independent attestors see a consistent growth signal—output that cannot be pasted across many clones—does the lease convert into full market rights. Operators who spin hundreds of empty identities produce identical, lifeless traces and are dropped.
